DomainGap.description:
A domain that could not be searched, and why.

**The third retrieval state.** `RetrievalSummary` already separates "we
looked and found nothing" from "we did not look"; this separates both from
"we *could not* look, because the instrument is not there." Without it a
consumer reading a thin `endpoint` narrative cannot tell a quiet host from a
host nobody was able to observe -- and the two justify opposite conclusions.

Not hypothetical. On `botsv3-coinhive-*` (2026-09-02) `edr` and `ndr` are
`{"disabled": true}` in `mcp_servers.json`, the Broker planned an
`edr_host_processes` step it had no tool to dispatch, and the siem subagents
themselves reported `gaps=['edr']`. Every one of those facts was recorded on
the fetch side and none of it crossed this boundary, so the Analyst Agent was
handed an endpoint judgement built entirely from SIEM process rows with no
indication that a dedicated endpoint instrument was expected and absent.

**A gap is not the same as a domain being irrelevant, and not the same as a
failure.** A missing `edr` does not mean endpoint questions went unanswered:
SIEM carries Sysmon process events and answered them on that run. What it
means is that the answer rests on one instrument rather than two, which is a
fact about confidence that only the Analyst Agent can price.

Deliberately NOT shown to the domain analysts. They are blind by
construction, and "no EDR instrument exists here" is a hint about what to
expect to find. It belongs on the record, not in a prompt.

advised_by.description: Families whose subagents flagged this one as able to close a gap they hit, via `SubagentAnswer.gaps`. Evidence that the gap mattered to the investigation rather than being a domain nobody wanted: a `not_configured` edr that three siem steps all asked for is a different fact from one nothing missed. Empty when the family was planned or dispatched but no subagent asked for it.
advised_by.title: Advised By

detail.description: The refusal message produced at the point of refusal, verbatim. Code-assembled, never model-authored -- it is the same string the fetch side already recorded on `SubtaskResult.reason` or `StepOutcome.reason`, carried across rather than re-derived, so the artifact and the run log cannot disagree about why.
detail.title: Detail

served_domains.description: The analysis domains this instrument would have supplied evidence for, from `subagent_analysts.routing.domains_for_family()` -- so `edr` names `endpoint`. A statement about what the missing instrument COULD have covered, not about what any query retrieved.
served_domains.title: Served Domains

unanswered_domains.description:
The subset of `served_domains` that received no evidence from ANY source. This is the field that resolves what the gap actually cost, and the two ends of it mean opposite things:

**Empty** -- something else covered every domain this instrument would have served, so the investigation is not missing an answer, only a second opinion. A missing `edr` whose `endpoint` domain was filled by SIEM process events lands here, which is the normal case in a SIEM-only deployment.

**Non-empty** -- those domains have no evidence AND the instrument that would most directly have produced it was unavailable, so "nothing happened" and "nobody could look" are indistinguishable for them. That ambiguity is the finding. It is recorded rather than resolved because resolving it needs a fact nobody here has: whether the environment was quiet, or merely unobserved. A consumer must not read an empty narrative for one of these domains as evidence of absence.
unanswered_domains.title: Unanswered Domains

DomainRecord.description:
One domain's judgement as it crosses to the Analyst Agent.

The wire projection of a `DomainFinding`. Same judgement, minus what is ours
rather than the consumer's, plus the evidence needed to check it.

Dropped from `DomainFinding`: `reasoning_trace`, `prompt_tokens`,
`generation_tokens`. The token counts are our telemetry. The trace is stronger
than that -- it is documented "persisted for audit, never re-fed", and putting
a model's private chain-of-thought into a contract handed to another model is
exactly re-feeding it. A projection rather than a `model_dump(exclude=...)` so
the published schema does not advertise fields the consumer must know to
ignore.

Added: `exhibits`. See `Exhibit`.

Renamed from `DomainJudgement` on 2026-10-09: this tier stopped judging on
2026-08-31, and the name kept saying it did. Only the type name changed; the
field data is the same, so older `findings.json` files load unchanged.
There is no verdict in it -- no `disposition`, no `confidence`, no stance.
See `Disposition` for where the deciding happens instead.

exhibits.description: The cited evidence, one entry per kept citation.
exhibits.title: Exhibits

facts.description: Lines computed in code over every routed row, never written by a model: the full paths behind each name the narrative uses, decoded encoded commands, interpreter and LOLBin command lines, and searches that returned no rows. Each block opens with its own header line.
facts.title: Facts

narrative.description: Plain English: what these rows show, in order. What happened, NOT what it means -- weighing it against the hypothesis is yours.
narrative.title: Narrative

summaries.description: One computed account per non-empty set routed to this domain, cited or not: totals, distinct counts, top and rarest values and the time range, calculated in code over every row. Not model-authored, so it holds what the narrative may have left out.
summaries.title: Summaries

DomainRecord.title: DomainRecord

Exhibit.description:
The actual rows behind one citation, rendered as the analyst saw them.

An `Evidence.id` is a pointer, and a pointer is only useful to a consumer
holding the evidence store. The Analyst Agent is a separate component and may
hold nothing; without the rows it can weigh a judgement only by trusting it.

Carrying every routed block instead would be the other failure -- on
`cli-20260825T100434` each domain was routed 32-35 blocks and cited one, so
the full pack is ~13-19k characters per domain against ~250 for the cited
blocks. Only what was cited travels.

`rows` is the same projected, `_sanitise`d text the domain analyst read, not
a re-render: an exhibit that formatted the rows differently from the evidence
the judgement was formed on would be a different exhibit.

`query` is the one thing here the analyst did *not* see, and deliberately so
-- see `formatting.format_result_set`.

evidence_ids.description: The `Evidence.id`s this block was projected from, for a consumer that does hold the store and wants the untruncated rows.
evidence_ids.title: Evidence Ids

query.description: The query that retrieved this set. Carried HERE rather than in `rows` because the two consumers differ: the domain analyst is blind to the hypothesis and a query written to test it leaks it (see `formatting.format_result_set`), while the Analyst Agent is not blind and cannot judge an empty set without knowing what was asked. Empty for a `reputation#N` exhibit, which is a reputation lookup rather than a search, and for exhibits written before this field existed.
query.title: Query

row_count.description: Rows in the underlying set, which is NOT the number rendered in `rows` -- exhibits are row-capped. Carried separately so a consumer can see that a cited set was empty, which is invisible from an id alone and which the grounding gate does not check for.
row_count.title: Row Count

rows.description: The rendered block: its `# header` line and the capped rows beneath it.
rows.title: Rows

Exhibit.title: Exhibit

RetrievalSummary.description:
What was looked for, and what the looking turned up.

The fetch side, projected for the consumer of `HypothesisFindings`. Without
it that contract carried three judgements and no account of the retrieval
behind them, so an `inconclusive` was unreadable: a domain reports it both
when the rows genuinely decide nothing and when nothing was ever retrieved
for it, and only the fetch record tells those apart. Deciding which one
happened is exactly the kind of call this contract exists to leave to the
Analyst Agent -- so it has to be given the facts to make it.

Deliberately not the whole `BrokerReport`: the consumer needs to know what
was asked and what came back, not to be able to re-run the fetch. Costs,
per-query records, raw `SubtaskResult`s and the classification stay in
`report.json`, joined by `HypothesisFindings.task_id`.

covered.description: Categories at least one subagent asserted it retrieved data for, unioned across dispatches. Model-authored (see `SiemAssessment.covered`) -- a claim about coverage, not a count of rows.
covered.title: Covered

dispatched.description: Families actually dispatched, observed at dispatch time.
dispatched.title: Dispatched

gaps.description: Domains that could not be searched at all, with the reason. See `DomainGap`: this is what tells a reader that a hypothesis was not searched in full because an instrument is missing, as distinct from a domain that was searched and had nothing to say. Empty means every family the investigation wanted was available -- NOT that every family was dispatched, which `dispatched` answers.
gaps.title: Gaps

not_covered.description: Categories that were asked for and that NO dispatch retrieved. Disjoint from `covered` by construction, and that subtraction is the point: a plain union of every subagent's own `not_covered` is noise, because a step scoped to one category honestly reports the other three as not covered. On `cli-20260825T100434` -- four siem steps, one category each -- the union put all four categories in BOTH lists, which tells a consumer nothing. One dispatch retrieving a category settles it for the investigation.
not_covered.title: Not Covered

unanswerable.description: Questions the Broker's plan stated no connected source can answer (B20).
unanswerable.title: Unanswerable

RetrievalSummary.title: RetrievalSummary

StepSummary.description:
What became of one planned fetch step, as the Analyst Agent needs to see it.

A projection of `contracts.subtask.StepOutcome`, code-assembled, carrying the
four facts that change how a judgement should be weighed and nothing else.
Dropped: `dispatches`, `refused_for_budget`, `status`, `reason` and the full
`FetchStep` -- dispatch counts and budget refusals are our operational
concern, not an input to reasoning about evidence.

`evaluated` is here and is load-bearing: `completed=False, evaluated=False`
means nobody ever judged this step, which is a different fact from
`completed=False, evaluated=True` ("ran and fell short"). See
`StepOutcome.evaluated`.
StepSummary.title: StepSummary

Unanswerable.description:
A question no connected source can answer, stated instead of fetched (B20).

On 89674d75 "asset inventory", "CrowdStrike telemetry" and "forensics tools"
questions were each run as Splunk searches, and the substitute rows came back
as if they answered them.

reason.description: A short noun phrase naming only the missing source or observable, e.g. 'asset inventory', 'file hash'. Never what other tools hold or the data shows.
reason.title: Reason

Unanswerable.title: Unanswerable

description:
Three blind domain judgements, attached to the hypothesis they never saw.

**The contract handed up to the Analyst Agent.** That agent is a separate
component, owned elsewhere; this is the boundary, and everything about the
shape follows from which side of it a decision belongs on.

What is here: what each domain's evidence shows, judged on the evidence
alone, and the means to verify that judgement against the rows behind it.

What is deliberately NOT here: any position on the hypothesis. There is no
`overall_stance` and no combiner, because deciding whether these findings
support or refute the hypothesis is the Analyst Agent's job. That absence is
the contract, not an omission -- `HypothesisAssessment` is the shape that
carries a decided stance, and it is a different shape for that reason.

The hypothesis appears here only as an id and, optionally, its prose. It is
the *attachment point*: the analysts formed their judgements without it, and
this is where the two are joined. A consumer that renders `hypothesis` into
a prompt MUST fence and escape it -- it is attacker-influenceable, the same
as `InvestigationContext.hypothesis`.

All three domains always appear in `findings`, including ones that got no
evidence. An empty domain appears with an **empty narrative and no
observations**, never silently omitted: "we looked and found nothing" and
"we did not look" are different facts, and the consumer cannot recover the
difference from a missing entry.

It can no longer recover it from the entry itself either, which is what
makes **`RetrievalSummary` the only signal separating those two facts.** An
empty domain used to at least say `inconclusive`; with the verdict gone
(2026-08-31) an empty finding is silent by construction, so `retrieval` is
no longer a supplement to `findings` -- it is the whole answer to "was
anything ever fetched for this domain?". A reader who takes it for a
redundant projection of the fetch side and deletes it takes that
distinction with it.

findings.description: One per analysis domain, including domains that saw no evidence.
findings.title: Findings

hypothesis.description: The hypothesis prose, if the producer had it. Carried so the artifact is self-describing rather than resolvable only against a live `InvestigationContext`. Attacker-influenceable -- fence and escape it before it reaches any prompt.
hypothesis.title: Hypothesis

retrieval.description: What the fetch side looked for and turned up. See `RetrievalSummary`: without it an `inconclusive` judgement cannot be told apart from a domain that was never given anything to read. Optional because artifacts written before this field exist and must still load.

run_id.description: The timestamped run directory these findings belong to. Unlike `HypothesisAssessment.run_id`, `gather()` sets this at construction wherever the caller knows it, rather than leaving it for the persistence layer to stamp on write. Stamping on write is fine for an artifact whose next stop is our own disk; this one is handed to another system and may never be persisted here at all, so a null `run_id` would make it unidentifiable at exactly the moment it crosses the boundary. Still optional, because a caller genuinely may not know it -- but it should be the exception now, not the default.
run_id.title: Run Id

task_id.description: The `BrokerReport.task_id` these findings were drawn from -- the join key back to `report.json`, and the prefix every `Evidence.id` in `citation_evidence` is built from. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-25-evidence-link-contract-design.md.
task_id.title: Task Id
